title: Tech hire skill titration and mentor shadow 9-day manual
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical playbook for converting mid-senior engineering candidates through an accelerated hands-on pairing + mentor-shadow experience (9 calendar days). Designed for time-sensitive hiring needs (backfill, surge hires, small-scale pods) where we need stronger signal than a take-home but less friction than a full onsite week.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: hiring managers, interview squad members, mentors (buddy), recruiting ops, and people-ops partners.
- Roles in this flow:
  - Hiring manager (HM): owns final decision, schedules pair sessions, sets project context.
  - Mentor/Buddy: assigned senior IC who shadows candidate pairing work and provides daily feedback.
  - Interviewer(s): one or two focused sessions (system design or debugging).
  - Recruiter: coordinates logistics, access, docs, and candidate experience.
  - People Ops: ensures offer timeline, equity calibration, and conversion checklist.

High-level goals:
1) Rapid, realistic signal on day-to-day collaboration ability and product-sense.
2) Reduce time-to-offer to within 3 business days post-run.
3) Improve candidate experience: transparent schedule, timely feedback, and a short retrospective.

Prerequisites (before Day 0):
- HM picks a lightweight pairing exercise or small microproject (2-4 hours) that mirrors everyday work (bug triage + fix, small feature toggle, infra script). Put tasks in a private repo with a short README.
- Mentor identified and given 2 hours prep slot with HM.
- Recruiter sends candidate a one-page primer: schedule, expectations, compensation band, and who they will meet.
- Access: candidate should get read-only repo access and an ephemeral dev container link (if using codespaces/Nix). If on-prem resources are needed, coordinate with infra 48h prior.

Day-by-day (compact):
Day 0 — logistics and primer (recruiter + HM)
- 30m call to review schedule and answer candidate Qs. Confirm timezone and dev environment.
- Send checklist to mentor about desired signals.
- TODO: update the primer template with current comp band.

Day 1 — pairing intro (2h)
- 15m context: HM explains the project and success criteria.
- 90m pairing: candidate + mentor work on microproject. Mentor uses 'observe-swap' pattern: 30m watch, 30m collaborate, 30m candidate drives while mentor prompts.
- 15m debrief: immediate gut-check and one-line notes.

Day 2 — focused problem (1.5h)
- 60-90m remote whiteboard/code exercise (systems thinking or debugging). Prefer live coding with tests.
- Interview rubric applied (see scoring below).

Day 3 — async followup (candidate has a 4h window)
- Candidate iterates on work, adds tests, writes a brief README describing choices.
- Mentor reviews asynchronously and leaves timestamped notes.

Day 4 — product-sense micro interview (1h)
- HM-led conversation rooted in the microproject: tradeoffs, metrics, rollout plan, observability.

Day 5 — team-fit conversation (45m)
- Peer chat with two engineers: culture, collaboration patterns, incident recall. Keep it conversational, let candidate ask questions about team rituals.

Day 6 — final pairing session (90m)
- Deeper pairing on a separate small bug/feature. Aim to see code ownership patterns and debugging under time pressure. Mentor writes consolidated notes.

Day 7 — pause / internal calibration
- Interviewers and HM sync for 60m. Capture signals, alignment, and near-term ramp plan.

Day 8 — compensation & ask check (recruiter + HM)
- If internal signals positive, recruiter prepares offer band and draft. HM drafts 30/60/90 plan for new hire.

Day 9 — offer decision and candidate feedback
- Final calibration and go/no-go. Recruiter communicates outcome and next steps. If moving to offer, target same-day verbal.

Scoring rubric (simple, numeric 1-5 per axis):
- Code fluency (1-5): correctness, idiomatic constructs, testing.
- Debugging & reasoning (1-5): reproduces bug, triage steps, root-cause thinking.
- Systems & product sense (1-5): tradeoff articulation, rollout strategy, metrics.
- Collaboration & communication (1-5): ability to accept feedback, explain decisions, pair etiquette.
- Ownership/readiness (1-5): quality of README, follow-through on async tasks.

Pass threshold recommendation: average >= 3.6 and no dimension <= 2. Notes: HM can override with strong ramp plan. For senior/stretch roles, look for 4+ across systems and collaboration.

Conversion checklist (pre-offer):
- Comp calibrated with compensation ops; equity bands verified.
- Reference check initiated (2 references).
- Manager draft: 30/60/90 ramp and onboarding buddy schedule.
- Access checklist: tooling, slack, repo access, infra tickets pre-created.
- Paperwork: verified authorization to work, relocation notes if applicable.

Mentor guide (what to look for during shadow):
- Does candidate ask clarifying Qs before coding?
- How do they handle ambiguous requirements?
- Rate of context uptake (how quickly do they grasp codebase patterns?).
- Test-first inclination and use of small automation.
- Timeboxing choices when stuck.

Manager check-ins (immediate after run):
- 30m HM+mentor debrief, capture 3 strengths and 3 risks.
- If considering offer, map top-3 ramp tasks and who on team will unblock them.

Candidate experience notes (for recruiter):
- Provide explicit timelines (we commit to decision within 72 hours of final session).
- Offer template with variable placeholders: title, level rationale, equity, target start date.
- Keep messages short and human; call within 24h for ambiguous outcomes.

Risk mitigation and alternatives:
- If candidate environment fails (envs, VPN), fall back to a screencast pairing or extended code exercise.
- If a mentor is unavailable, rotate to two shorter sessions with different peers.

Templates (quick copy snippets):
- Primer email subject: "Redwood — 9-day pairing plan and what to expect"
- Quick mentor note: "Focus on collaboration signals (asks/clarifies), test coverage, and timeboxing. Please add 5 bullet points after each session."
- Debrief format: "Strength 1 | Strength 2 | Risk 1 | Risk 2 | Recommendation (hire/hold/decline)"

Post-hire onboarding tie-ins (if offer accepted):
- Convert microproject into a first-week ramp ticket (pair with mentor on day 2 post-start).
- Mentor becomes onboarding buddy for first 30 days; weekly 1:1 sticky slots.
- Add candidate notes to hiring doc (signals and ramp plan) for next manager.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize microprojects across teams (pros: easier calibration; cons: less realistic work)? Decision: HM-level opt-in, People Ops to maintain a short repo of templates.
- Add an automated scheduling template in Workflows to reduce recruiter overhead.

Appendix — quick scoring form (copy into Google Form):
[fields] Candidate name, Role, Date, Session type, Code fluency 1-5, Debugging 1-5, Systems 1-5, Collaboration 1-5, Ownership 1-5, Free notes (3 bullets).

Notes to self:
- Track NPS of candidate experience for this flow (post-process survey) and iterate every quarter.
- Pilot this with 6 hires and measure time-to-productive-week-6 metric.

End of doc. If anyone wants a shorter 3-day variant we can sketch a compressed run (3 pairing blocks + 1 async followup).
